core/classified-by.purpose: Elements classified under a taxonomy concept or any concept beneath it.
core/classified-by.answers: The membership of a taxonomy branch, whichever scheme it belongs to.
core/classified-by.does_not_prove: That unclassified elements fall outside the branch.

CONCEPT_IRI.description: SKOS concept at the top of the branch

core/coverage-gaps.purpose: Elements of a type with no value for an expected predicate.
core/coverage-gaps.answers: Where the models are silent about something you expected.
core/coverage-gaps.does_not_prove: That the real thing lacks the property. Nobody recorded it.

core/define-term.purpose: Explain each resource a term matches: definition, type, owning model, immediate relationships.
core/define-term.answers: What this dataset says a term means, and how ambiguous the term is.
core/define-term.does_not_prove: That a definition is true, current or agreed. It is text somebody typed in a modelling tool.

core/dependents-direct.purpose: Transitive dependents through named direct predicates.
core/dependents-direct.answers: Everything reaching an element at any depth along a chosen predicate set.
core/dependents-direct.does_not_prove: Impact, or completeness beyond the predicates named.

PREDICATE_PATH.description: direct predicates to follow, from core/discover-relationship-types

core/dependents-qualified.purpose: What reaches an element within two hops, via the qualified form.
core/dependents-qualified.answers: Bounded incoming dependency paths, with the relationship types on each.
core/dependents-qualified.does_not_prove: Impact. Reachability in a model is not blast radius.

core/discover-predicates.purpose: Predicates in use, with frequency and object kind.
core/discover-predicates.answers: Exact predicate spellings, including house fields with no core role.
core/discover-predicates.does_not_prove: That a predicate means what its local name suggests.

core/discover-relationship-types.purpose: Relationship types present, with counts and the endpoint types they join.
core/discover-relationship-types.answers: Which relationship kinds this dataset actually uses.
core/discover-relationship-types.does_not_prove: What the metamodel permits. This is what was modelled.

core/element-detail.purpose: Every predicate and object on one resource, with its graph.
core/element-detail.answers: What the dataset actually says about an element, in exact spelling.
core/element-detail.does_not_prove: Completeness. Absent here means absent from the models.

core/elements-by-type.answers: The population of a class, with labels and native ids.
core/elements-by-type.does_not_prove: That the type is the element's only type. Elements are multi-typed.

core/graph-provenance.purpose: What produced each named graph, from which source, and when.
core/graph-provenance.answers: Whether every graph in the dataset can be accounted for, or just the graphs whose IRI matches GRAPH_MATCH.
core/graph-provenance.does_not_prove: That a graph is complete, or that its source is current.

GRAPH_MATCH.description: narrow to graphs whose IRI contains this fragment: a notation slug, a model id, or a graph role such as graph/semantic. Empty means every graph

core/identity-audit.purpose: Cross-source identity assertions, and which kind each is.
core/identity-audit.answers: Which elements are linked across tools, by correspondence or by identity.
core/identity-audit.does_not_prove: That unlisted elements have no counterpart. Identity is authored.

core/inventory.purpose: Named graphs, types and counts. Run first, every session.
core/inventory.answers: What is loaded, from which graphs, and how much of each type.
core/inventory.does_not_prove: That the dataset is complete. A low count is usually a partial export.

core/inventory-summary.purpose: Notations present, with model, graph and concept counts. Use on a large dataset.
core/inventory-summary.answers: How much of each notation is loaded, in one screen.
core/inventory-summary.does_not_prove: Completeness. A missing notation may never have been converted, or a merge may have dropped it.

core/label-collisions.purpose: Elements sharing a normalised label across different models. Identity CANDIDATES only.
core/label-collisions.answers: Where the same name appears in more than one model, with each side's type and model.
core/label-collisions.does_not_prove: Identity. Same label is not same system: it may be one thing modelled twice, two things, or a thing and a record about it.
core/label-collisions.caveat: core/label-collisions returns identity CANDIDATES, not identity assertions. A shared label is not evidence that two resources are the same thing. Cross-tool identity here is authored and human-reviewed: core/identity-audit reads those assertions, and this template makes none.

core/lifecycle.purpose: Element-level lifecycle status, where any notation records it.
core/lifecycle.answers: Which elements carry a status, and what it is.
core/lifecycle.does_not_prove: Coverage. Lifecycle is sparse and notation-specific.

core/models.purpose: Models present, the metamodel each conforms to, and its source.
core/models.answers: Which notations contributed, and when each model was converted.
core/models.does_not_prove: That a model is current. A conversion timestamp is not an as-at date.

core/neighbours-qualified.purpose: Direct relationships touching an element, via the qualified form.
core/neighbours-qualified.answers: What an element relates to, in both directions, with the relationship kind.
core/neighbours-qualified.does_not_prove: Runtime dependency, criticality or failure propagation.

core/neighbours-reified.purpose: Relationships touching an element, naming the unqualified predicate as well as the class.
core/neighbours-reified.answers: What an element relates to, in both directions, with the predicate the bridge names.
core/neighbours-reified.does_not_prove: Runtime dependency. And one hop only: paths cannot traverse triple terms.

core/orphans.purpose: Elements taking part in no relationship.
core/orphans.answers: Where the model has islands, as a data-quality reading.
core/orphans.does_not_prove: That an element is unused or safe to remove.

core/provenance.purpose: Source file, converter, and timestamps behind an element's model.
core/provenance.answers: Where a fact came from, so a claim becomes evidence.
core/provenance.does_not_prove: That the source model is current, correct or approved.

core/reified-predicates.purpose: Unqualified predicates exposed by the RDF 1.2 reification bridge, per qualified class.
core/reified-predicates.answers: The predicate a relationship stands for, which the qualified class alone does not carry.
core/reified-predicates.does_not_prove: That the predicate is asserted. A triple term is not a triple, and property paths do not traverse it.

core/reifies-audit.purpose: Qualified relationships whose triple term is missing or disagrees with arch:source/arch:target.
core/reifies-audit.answers: Whether the two halves of each relationship agree with each other.
core/reifies-audit.does_not_prove: Correctness. A relationship wrong in both halves agrees with itself and passes.

core/resolve-element.purpose: Resolve a name a user typed to candidate IRIs, best candidate first.
core/resolve-element.answers: Which resources match a term by name, alias or native id, ranked by how much of the value matched (?rank) and by which of the three matched (?matched).
core/resolve-element.does_not_prove: That the top match is the one meant. Ask when the choice changes the answer.

TERM.description: name or fragment the user typed

LIMIT.description: maximum rows. A full page means candidates were discarded: the envelope reports truncated, so raise this rather than reading the page as the whole answer

core/resolve-model.purpose: Resolve a phrase to a model, as against a concept inside one.
core/resolve-model.answers: Which models match by title, name, native id, description, source file, status or notation, ranked exact then prefix then substring.
core/resolve-model.does_not_prove: That the top-ranked model is the one meant, or that it is current. Rank is string similarity only.

TERM.description: name or fragment the user typed

core/traceability.purpose: Paths of one or two hops between two kinds of element.
core/traceability.answers: Which elements of one type connect to which of another, and how.
core/traceability.does_not_prove: That an unlisted pair is unconnected. Deeper paths are out of scope.

core/validation-summary.purpose: SHACL verdict with violations by severity and shape, from a report in the dataset.
core/validation-summary.answers: What a loaded SHACL report says, and how much it covered.
core/validation-summary.does_not_prove: Soundness. A verdict without an evaluated count means nothing.

core/view-contents.answers: What one view depicts, with each element's label, native id and types.
core/view-contents.does_not_prove: That the diagram is current, or that an element absent from it is absent from the architecture.

VIEW_IRI.description: the view to read, from core/views

core/view-contents-semantic.purpose: Which elements a diagram places, read from the semantic graph.
core/view-contents-semantic.answers: What one view depicts, from the one-hop arch:inView edge rather than a node in the views graph. The route that survives output published without geometry.
core/view-contents-semantic.does_not_prove: That the diagram is current, or that an element absent from it is absent from the architecture. It also says nothing about where on the canvas anything sits - use core/view-contents where the views graph exists.

VIEW_IRI.description: the view to read, from core/views

core/view-contents-semantic.caveat: Read from arch:inView, so this reports which view presents an element and not where it is drawn. An element placed twice on one view is reported once.

core/view-diff.purpose: Set difference between two views, by placed element.
core/view-diff.answers: Which elements one diagram places and the other does not, in either or both directions.
core/view-diff.does_not_prove: That a difference between diagrams is a difference in the architecture. Views are editorial.

DIRECTION.description: which side to report; symmetric reports both differences and never the shared elements

core/view-usage.answers: Where an element has been drawn, and under which viewpoint.
core/view-usage.does_not_prove: That an undrawn element is unimportant.

core/view-usage-semantic.purpose: Which diagrams depict an element, read from the semantic graph.
core/view-usage-semantic.answers: Where an element has been drawn and under which viewpoint, from the one-hop arch:inView edge rather than a node in the views graph.
core/view-usage-semantic.does_not_prove: That an undrawn element is unimportant. It returns no node, so it cannot distinguish two drawings of one element on one view.
core/view-usage-semantic.caveat: Returns no node column, unlike core/view-usage. Each view is reported once however many times the element is drawn on it.

core/views.purpose: Views present, their viewpoint, and how many nodes each places.
core/views.answers: What diagrams exist and how substantial they are.
core/views.does_not_prove: Quality or currency of a diagram.

notation/archimate/layer-crossing.purpose: Relationships that cross ArchiMate layers, grouped by layer pair.
notation/archimate/layer-crossing.answers: Where realisation and serving cross layers, and how often.
notation/archimate/layer-crossing.does_not_prove: That a crossing is correct, or that a missing one is a gap. Layer is inferred from class names.

notation/backstage/ownership.purpose: Backstage entities and the group or user that owns them.
notation/backstage/ownership.answers: Who is recorded as owning what, with lifecycle state.
notation/backstage/ownership.does_not_prove: Accountability. spec.owner is what somebody wrote in a file.

notation/bpmn/process-components.purpose: What takes part in a BPMN model, grouped by kind of participant.
notation/bpmn/process-components.answers: Where work arrives, what is automated, what a person does, the participants, the data touched, and where it ends.
notation/bpmn/process-components.does_not_prove: That any of it runs. A ServiceTask is a modelled intent, not a deployed service.

MODEL_IRI.description: the BPMN model, from core/models or core/resolve-model

notation/bpmn/process-flow.purpose: Sequence flows of one BPMN process, as edges.
notation/bpmn/process-flow.answers: Which steps follow which, with the flow element types.
notation/bpmn/process-flow.does_not_prove: Runtime order. Gateways branch; these are edges, not a path.

notation/c4/containers.purpose: C4 elements with type, technology and containing parent.
notation/c4/containers.answers: The container and component structure of a C4 model.
notation/c4/containers.does_not_prove: Deployment. A container is a modelled unit, not a running instance.

notation/leanix/factsheets.purpose: LeanIX fact sheets with status, completion and lifecycle phase.
notation/leanix/factsheets.answers: What the inventory holds and how filled-in each record is.
notation/leanix/factsheets.does_not_prove: That a fact sheet's subject exists, or that its content is right. A fact sheet is a record about a thing.
